requirement_paraphrase: SAIL from final GRC and residual ARC: e.g. GRC 5 with ARC a/b/c/d gives IV/IV/IV/VI; GRC 6 gives V/V/V/VI; GRC 7 gives VI; GRC above 7 is certified category. SAIL sets OSO robustness levels and evidence expected.
For machinery in Annex I Part A categories, manufacturer must use module B (EU type-examination) plus C, or module H (full quality assurance), or module G (unit verification).
applies_to: Annex I Part A categories (trigger: product falls in Part A)

requirement_paraphrase: Law firm summary: safety functions and settings must not be easily modifiable beyond the manufacturer's risk analysis limits, incl. by machine learning; safety decision data kept at least one year; control system logs of interventions in safety software kept at least five years after modified software upload.
applies_to: Machinery with control systems, incl. self-learning

requirement_paraphrase: Substantial modification (Art. 3(16)) is a physical or digital change made after placing on the market, not foreseen or planned by the manufacturer, that creates a new hazard or increases an existing risk and requires added guards/protective devices that change the safety control system, or additional measures for stability/mechanical strength. Under Art. 18(1)-(2) the person making it is treated as manufacturer, must declare conformity on its own responsibility and apply the Art. 25(2), (3) or (4) procedure. Art. 18(3): a non-professional user who substantially modifies own machinery for personal use is not treated as a manufacturer." Art. 18(1) also brings the Art. 10 manufacturer duties.
applies_to: Persons modifying machinery (incl. software-driven change); non-professional personal-use modifiers excluded (18(3))

requirement_paraphrase: UL 4600 Ed. 3 (2023): safety argument for vehicles operating autonomously without expected human intervention; scope includes foreseeable misuse and physical attacks, and detailed information security is largely out of scope (catalogue summary; clause numbers not seen).
applies_to: Autonomous vehicles/products (UL 4600 is not itself law; may be required by contract or referenced by a regulator)

requirement_paraphrase: Defines Goal Structuring Notation syntax and semantics and gives guidance on building and evaluating goal structures. No requirement that a product use it.
Manufacturer must ensure machinery is designed and built to meet the Annex III essential health and safety requirements before placing on market or putting into service.
applies_to: Manufacturers of machinery and related products

requirement_paraphrase: Title and scope only: GCAA CAR-UAC covers commercial and governmental unmanned aircraft operations in the UAE (Issue 02 listed).

Remote pilot in command must report to the FAA within 10 calendar days an operation causing serious injury or loss of consciousness, or damage to property other than the UA unless repair cost and fair market value are both $500 or less.
applies_to: US small UAS operators under Part 107

requirement_paraphrase: Robustness = lower of integrity and assurance level. Low assurance: applicant declares; medium: applicant supplies evidence (testing/operational data); high: verified by a competent third party. Three robustness levels (low, medium, high).

Reported to require a data storage system, reporting of critical events with follow-up reports within 30 days where required, and annual safety data; the specific event categories were not seen in the source.

instrument: ISO 3691-4 Industrial trucks - driverless trucks and systems
requirement_paraphrase: Table of contents shows climatic-condition and high-temperature clauses; requirement text not accessed.

An AI system is high-risk if it is a safety component of, or is itself, a product covered by Annex I legislation AND that product must undergo third-party conformity assessment under that legislation.
applies_to: Robots, drones, machines whose AI is a safety component of an Annex I product requiring third-party assessment

instrument: Implementing Reg (EU) 2019/947 (as fetched from EUR-Lex PDF)
requirement_paraphrase: Three operation categories: open (no prior authorisation/declaration), specific (operational authorisation, model-club authorisation or declaration in Art. 5(5) cases), certified (UAS certification, operator certification, licensing where applicable).
applies_to: UAS operators in EU Member States

instrument: Implementing Reg (EU) 2019/947 (as fetched from EUR-Lex PDF) Annex Part B
requirement_paraphrase: Authorisation application (UAS.SPEC.030) is based on the Art. 11 risk assessment and includes registration number, accountable manager (or operator name), the risk assessment, proposed mitigations in sufficient detail, an operations manual where risk and complexity require one, and insurance confirmation where required by law. Operator (UAS.SPEC.050) must establish procedures for safety, security, unlawful interference, data protection (DPIA where required) and noise/emissions, designate competent remote pilots, train staff, and keep records of operations.

Deployers must assign trained, authorised human overseers, monitor operation against instructions, stop use and notify provider on risk, report serious incidents, and keep automatically generated logs at least six months.
Title and scope only: GCAA CAR-UAC covers commercial and governmental unmanned aircraft operations in the UAE (Issue 02 listed).
Title and scope only: GCAA CAR-UAC covers commercial and governmental unmanned aircraft operations in the UAE (Issue 02 listed).

instrument: Defeaters and Eliminative Argumentation in Assurance 2.0
requirement_paraphrase: Argues that assurance cases should record defeaters (doubts) and investigate them; a case is closed only with no unsupported claims and no active defeaters.
Series scope: safety-related E/E systems in series-production road vehicles (excl. mopeds); excludes hazards such as electric shock or fire unless caused by E/E malfunction.

Part A list reported to include safety components with fully or partially self-evolving behaviour using machine learning to ensure safety functions, and embedded systems with such components when not separately marketed. Conformity route for Part A categories under Art. 25(2): module B plus C, module H or module G (EUR-Lex extraction, 2026-10-12). The Annex I entry itself and its number remain unverified.
applies_to: ML-based safety components and machinery embedding them

requirement_paraphrase: Commission news page states high-risk rules for Annex III systems apply from 2 December 2027 and for Annex I systems from 2 August 2028; dates for new Art. 5 bans and Arts. 102-110 are not given there.

Before placing on the market or putting into service, manufacturer prepares Annex IV Part A technical documentation, completes Art. 25 conformity assessment (or has it done), then draws up Art. 21 EU declaration and affixes CE marking.

instrument: IEC 61496-3 ESPE using active opto-electronic devices responsive to diffuse reflection (AOPDDR)
requirement_paraphrase: Preview states the document does not address requirements and tests for outdoor application. Environmental requirements and tests exist (clauses 4.3 and 5.4 appear only as headings in the preview; IEC 60068-2-14:2023 is a normative reference) and light-interference tests are listed. That dust or sunlight are therefore outside the tested envelope is interpretation, not text seen.
applies_to: Safety laser scanners / person-detection sensors for machinery

requirement_paraphrase: Reported to assume ADS software does not change driving behaviour through in-vehicle learning, and to require cybersecurity controls, software update processes and remote termination capability.

CEN-CENELEC overview says new definitions (autonomous mobile machinery, supervisor, supervisory function), a new supervisory function section, control system performing safety functions itself despite remote supervision, movement accounting for area risks, additions in 3.3.3 and 3.3.5 (no wording), and a new 3.6.3.3 on autonomous mobile machinery (no content).
Safety requirements for industrial robot applications and cells across design, integration, commissioning, operation, maintenance, decommissioning and disposal, plus information needed at each stage.
applies_to: Integrators and users of robot cells

requirement_paraphrase: SORA is a recommended methodology to establish confidence that a specific operation can be conducted safely: ConOps evaluation, categorisation into six SAIL levels, then recommended operational safety objectives per SAIL.

edition_or_version: Guidance v1.1 (file SACE_v1_1.pdf); fetch tool reported 'July 2026'
requirement_paraphrase: Eight-stage system-level process: operating context, hazardous scenarios, safe operating concept, safety requirements, design, hazardous failures, out-of-context operation (ODM boundary and minimum risk strategy), verification; each with a GSN pattern; ML components handled via AMLAS.
applies_to: Autonomous systems in complex environments (incl. robots, drones)

requirement_paraphrase: Machinery certified under an EU cybersecurity certification scheme (Reg. (EU) 2019/881) is presumed compliant with Annex III sections 1.1.9 and 1.2.1 (protection against corruption; safety and reliability of control systems) insofar as the certificate covers them.

edition_or_version: Reg 2024/1689 as amended by Reg 2026/1744 (text from unofficial reproduction)
requirement_paraphrase: Instructions for use must state accuracy levels and metrics, robustness, cybersecurity, factors affecting them, foreseeable misuse risks, dataset information, human oversight measures, hardware needs, lifespan and maintenance/update frequency, and log-handling mechanisms.

instrument: Dubai Executive Council Resolution No. (3) of 2019 (testing autonomous vehicles)
requirement_paraphrase: Testing requires an RTA contract and Authorisation; RTA sets safety standards for each test phase and designates roads and times; establishments file periodic stage reports and carry insurance.

Catalogue abstract: general argument framework and guidance to achieve freedom from unreasonable risk from functional insufficiencies, covering design, verification, validation and operation-phase activities.
applies_to: Series-production road vehicles with E/E systems (driving automation levels 1-5, emergency intervention); not robots

requirement_paraphrase: Blog lists topics the standard covers: dependability, V&V, tool qualification, COTS and legacy components, lifecycle, maintenance, metrics/SPIs, conformance and independent assessment; three-step claim/argument/evidence structure.

Documented quality management system covering compliance strategy, design/development/testing procedures, standards used, data management, risk management, post-market monitoring, serious incident reporting, resources and accountability. Art. 17(2) replaced by point (11): implementation proportionate to provider size, keeping the required level of rigour and protection.

instrument: Dubai Law No. (4) of 2020 regulating drone activity in Dubai
edition_or_version: Issued 2020; effective on Official Gazette publication per Media Office
requirement_paraphrase: All drone-related operations in Dubai and its free zones require a Dubai Civil Aviation Authority licence; owners register drones with DCAA; operational safety certificate before flying; permits for drone infrastructure; privacy and recording limits; imprisonment/fines for violations.
applies_to: Drone operators, manufacturers, owners in Dubai

requirement_paraphrase: C1 geo-awareness function must load airspace data, warn the pilot of potential breach, and (per extraction) flag when its positioning is unreliable.

High-risk systems need appropriate accuracy, robustness and cybersecurity throughout their lifecycle; declared accuracy metrics; resilience to errors and faults (redundancy or fail-safe allowed); mitigation of feedback loops for learning systems; protection against data poisoning, adversarial inputs and model flaws.

instrument: ISO 34503 Specification for operational design domain
requirement_paraphrase: Specifies a hierarchical taxonomy of operating conditions and a format for defining an ADS ODD; mainly L3/L4; excludes basic test procedures for ODD attributes and monitoring requirements.

instrument: AMLAS Guidance on Assurance of ML in Autonomous Systems
requirement_paraphrase: AMLAS expects data requirements covering relevance, completeness, accuracy and balance, with data validation results justifying gaps, and documents the operating environment; the named justification report and the word must were not confirmed.

instrument: Commission Implementing Decision C(2025) 129 final (standardisation request for Reg. 2023/1230), Annexes 1-2
requirement_paraphrase: Commission Implementing Decision C(2025) 129 final of 20 Jan 2025 requests CEN and CENELEC standards under Reg 2023/1230, including for self-evolving or ML based safety functions, autonomous mobile machinery and robotics; Phase 1 deadline 20 Jan 2026, Phase 2 20 Jan 2034 (one item has only the 2034 deadline).
applies_to: Standards bodies; shows expected future harmonised standards

requirement_paraphrase: Machinery not in Annex I uses module A (internal production control).

instrument: Regulation (EU) No 376/2014 Reporting of occurrences in civil aviation
edition_or_version: Consolidated 2018-09-11 (EUR-Lex); UK retained version also read
requirement_paraphrase: Regulation 376/2014 (original 2014 text at this URL) requires listed persons to report occurrences within 72 hours and organisations to run mandatory and voluntary reporting systems; the text does not expressly address unmanned aircraft. Edition is the original OJ text, not the 2018 consolidation or UK retained version.
applies_to: Persons and organisations in EU civil aviation

requirement_paraphrase: Title and scope only: GCAA CAR-UAEX covers unmanned aircraft experimentation operations in the UAE (Issue 02 Corrected listed).
applies_to: R&D and academic UA operators in UAE (relevant to prototype drone/robot testing)

requirement_paraphrase: Testing must use metrics and probabilistic thresholds defined in advance and suited to the intended purpose; testing may include real-world testing, which must meet Art 57 or 60 conditions; testing is done throughout development and in any event before placing on the market or putting into service.

instrument: NHTSA Standing General Order 2021-01 (Third Amended) crash reporting
requirement_paraphrase: Named manufacturers/operators must report ADS and L2 ADAS crashes: most severe within 5 days, others monthly; ADS thresholds stricter than ADAS; crash within 30 seconds of system use.
applies_to: Named entities in US (ADS L3-5 and L2 ADAS)

instrument: EASA AMC & GM to Reg (EU) 2019/947 (Annex to ED Decision 2025/018/R)
requirement_paraphrase: Before SORA the operator should check whether the operation is open category, covered by a standard scenario with class-labelled UAS, or covered by an EASA-published PDRA; only otherwise run SORA.

instrument: Implementing Reg (EU) 2019/947 (as fetched from EUR-Lex PDF)
requirement_paraphrase: Authority evaluates the risk assessment and robustness of mitigations across all flight phases, grants authorisation only if safety objectives, mitigations and competence are adequate, must refuse with reasons otherwise, and states scope, conditions, limitations and reporting duties.

Art. 40: design, production and maintenance must be certified if the UAS has a characteristic dimension of 3 m or more and is designed for operation over assemblies of people, or is designed to carry people, or to carry dangerous goods requiring high robustness; or where a specific-category authorisation risk assessment finds the risk cannot be mitigated without certification. Art. 41: operators from third countries must follow Implementing Reg. 2019/947 in single European sky airspace; competent authority is that of the first Member State of operation.
applies_to: Certified-category UAS; non-EU operators flying in EU

Provides a UML data model and exchange formats (e.g. YAML, OpenSCENARIO DSL) for describing operational, current and target operational domains of ADS.

instrument: ICAO MID CNS SG/15 WP08 (Saudi Arabia) national GNSS monitoring
requirement_paraphrase: Proposes a national GNSS signal monitoring and reporting system for the Jeddah FIR and a regional RFI database.

A category goes into Annex I Part A if it presents a serious inherent risk and at least one of four conditions in Art. 6(7) applies: missing standards, recurring serious accidents, recurring misapplication of standards, or uncertainty in risk assessment methods for new technologies.

For high-risk AI related to Annex I Section B products, only Art. 6(1), Art. 60a and Arts. 102-112 apply; Arts. 57-59 apply only insofar as high-risk requirements are incorporated into the Section B legislation. Art. 2(13), new, lets specific requirements in Arts 9-15 and 17-25 be limited for Art. 6(1) systems where Section A law gives equivalent protection; delegated acts by 2 Aug 2027. Also note: the machinery reading depends on Annex I placement, which was not confirmed officially.

instrument: Dubai RTA executive regulations for Law No. 9 of 2023 (autonomous vehicles)
edition_or_version: Gulf News article last updated 13 Dec 2025; Bracewell cites Administrative Resolution No. 939 of 2025
requirement_paraphrase: Per Gulf News (13 Dec 2025), autonomous vehicles must meet seven technical and operational criteria for approval, including a manufacturer's certificate of successful road trials in its country of origin or another jurisdiction, evidence of conformity with relevant UAE or Gulf standards, and operational tests in Dubai demonstrating safety under local climatic conditions, with trial data shared with the RTA and identified issues addressed. Operators must notify the RTA of technical faults immediately and maintain integrated, secure electronic records of all operational data that may not be altered or deleted without prior RTA approval.

With vision unaided other than corrective lenses, the remote pilot in command, the visual observer (if used) and the person manipulating the controls must be able to see the aircraft throughout flight to know its location, determine attitude/altitude/direction, observe airspace for traffic or hazards, and determine it does not endanger others' life or property; under 107.31(b) this must be exercised by the RPIC and controls person, or by a visual observer.
Title and scope only: GCAA CAR-UAC covers commercial and governmental unmanned aircraft operations in the UAE (Issue 02 listed).

instrument: UK CAA guidance on GNSS jamming (via SUAS News report)
requirement_paraphrase: Reports that CAA advises operators not to rely solely on satellite navigation during known jamming trials (be ready for alternatives such as dead reckoning), notes jamming can disable drone return-to-home and digital geofencing, and urges pilots to report jamming not announced in advance.

UNECE WP.29 adopted (24 Jun 2026, reported) a regulation for fully driverless ADS built on a safety case and safety management system; manufacturers must show no unreasonable safety risk using credible testing, including validated virtual environments, proving-ground testing and real-world trials, plus in-service monitoring/reporting and a Data Storage System for Automated Driving. (Blog does not mention ODD or SAE levels.)

instrument: RTA Administrative Resolution No. (939) of 2025 (AV executive rules)
edition_or_version: Issued 10 Nov 2025; effective on Official Gazette publication (Art. 16)
requirement_paraphrase: Covers light/heavy autonomous vehicles, buses, autonomous equipment and machinery, motorcycles. Art. 3 safety assessment: manufacturer-country compliance certificate, public-road test certificate, UAE conformity certificate, local operational test runs with data to RTA, design safety showing, RTA-approved speed/lane/zone system. Art. 4 emergency communication with Operator. Art. 14: operators notify malfunctions, store operational data securely, apply secure software updates.
